official.deadline_note: The European Commission publishes no central student deadline: 'In most cases, you should submit your application between October and January for courses starting the following academic year', and each master's own website holds the exact dates. Czech example - the Czech-coordinated EPS (Vaclav Havel) programme's 2026-2028 round: admission window opened 1 November, applications received by midnight CET 28 February 2026 were automatically treated as scholarship applications, a second 1 March - 30 April window accepted self-funding applicants only, and results were announced 30 April; that scholarship round is now closed and the next self-funding window opens 1 November 2026. (The 12 February 17:00 Brussels-time date in the Programme Guide is the institutional call deadline for consortia, ERASMUS-EDU-2026-PEX-EMJM-MOB, not a student deadline.)
official.application_cycle: Annual Erasmus Mundus Joint Master rounds; applications are usually submitted between October and January for courses starting the following academic year (the 2027/2028 cycle would open from about October 2026), with each consortium running its own window.
official.status_note: The scheme is permanently open with rolling per-programme rounds: 'Students apply directly to the institution running their chosen programme' and 'a new batch of selected Erasmus Mundus Masters is added to the list each year'. Round-level status must be read on the individual programme's own website - e.g. the Czech-coordinated EPS programme states its 2026-2028 scholarship window is CLOSED, that it received new EU funding giving 'more than 50 scholarships' for 2026-2031, and that scholarships 'will be available until the year 2031'.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Programme Guide: 'Selected projects cannot charge student application fees. Moreover, projects cannot charge tuition fees or other mandatory costs related to student participation in the course to Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders.' Student-facing EC page: 'Scholarships cover your participation costs'. Czech-coordinated EPS consortium: 'The EMJMD Scholarship fully covers the Tuition Fee for each semester of the EPS Programme for the two-year standard study period' - Programme Country track 'Full coverage of the Tuition Fee (11,000 EUR)', Partner Country track 'Full coverage of the Tuition Fee (18 000 EUR)', with the fee 'automatically deducted from the Scholarship by the Institution'.
official.funding_period: per month, for the full duration of the Master
benefits: 'Full scholarships are available for the best students' and 'Scholarships cover your participation costs and contribute to travel, visa, a living allowance' (EC, Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters students page)

'The scholarship will be a contribution to the costs incurred by the beneficiary students and shall cover travel, visa, installation and subsistence costs' (Erasmus+ Programme Guide, Lot 1 student scholarships)

'The scholarship is calculated as: 1 400 Euros/month x DS' where DS = duration of the Master programme, for 12, 18 or 24 months, awarded pro-rata of the actual number of days (Erasmus+ Programme Guide)

Czech-coordinated EPS consortium (Vaclav Havel Joint Master, Charles University): 'Living Allowances up to 24 months: 1,400 EUR per month (33,600 EUR)' plus full tuition ('11,000 EUR' Programme Country track / 'EUR 18.000' Partner Country track)

'The EPS Consortium also covers insurance for scholarship holders' and 'Scholarship fully covers all the activities during the EPS study period (four semesters), including classes, guest lectures' (Czech-coordinated consortium)
Additional support for enrolled students with disabilities as special-needs unit costs from EUR 3 000 up to EUR 60 000 per student (Erasmus+ Programme Guide)
eligibility: 'have a bachelor's degree (first degree), or be in your last year of bachelor studies' and 'graduate before the master's programme starts'; applicants may also apply if they demonstrate a bachelor's equivalent level of learning officially recognised in the degree-awarding country (EC students page)

'EMJM scholarships can be offered to students from all over the world' and 'Students from all over the world are welcome'; 'your nationality does not affect your eligibility' (Erasmus+ Programme Guide / EC student-facing pages)
'Students who have previously obtained an EMJM scholarship are not eligible to apply for an additional scholarship under the EMJM.' (Erasmus+ Programme Guide)
'The scholarship is awarded for full-time enrolment' and 'During this period, the scholarship can only be awarded in full, and to full-time students.' (Erasmus+ Programme Guide)

Programme Country track: the student is a national of an Erasmus+ Programme Country, or is ordinarily resident / has carried out their main activity (studies, training or work) for more than a total of 12 months over the last five years in any Programme Country before the scholarship submission deadline. Partner Country track: must NOT be a national of an Erasmus+ Programme Country and must not be ordinarily resident nor have carried out their main activity for more than 12 months over the last five years in any Programme Country (Czech-coordinated EPS consortium rules).

Geographic balance rule: 'no more than 10% of the total number of scholarships awarded during project implementation should be awarded to candidates from the same nationality', alongside compulsory physical mobility for every enrolled student - a minimum of two study periods in two countries, at least one of which must be an EU Member State or third country associated to the Programme, and both different from the student's country of residence at enrolment (Erasmus+ Programme Guide)
requirements: A first higher education degree, or a recognised equivalent level of learning according to national legislation and practices in the degree-awarding countries/institutions (Erasmus+ Programme Guide)
Documented English proficiency at the level set by the individual consortium - the Czech-coordinated EPS consortium requires 'C1; CAE; IELTS 7.0; TOEFL 95' for non-native English speakers
Full-time enrolment for the whole Master programme; a reduced scholarship duration applies only with recognition of prior learning and has a minimum of one academic year (Erasmus+ Programme Guide)
Completion of the consortium's own application file, including the supplementary questionnaire on study-track preferences (Czech-coordinated EPS consortium)
Formal commitment through a signed Student Agreement with the consortium upon enrolment, under the template published on the programme's website (Erasmus+ Programme Guide)
documents: Translated copy of a diploma showing completed Bachelor's or Master's studies (or confirmation of ongoing studies in the academic year they will be completed), plus a copy of a second diploma - a second completed Bachelor's OR the High School diploma
Translated transcript of marks and academic results from both previous studies

Identity and residence documents: copy of passport, plus proof of place of residence issued within 12 months before the submission deadline (ID, driver's licence, another PRADO-listed document, or a certificate from the candidate's place of work, study or training)
Curriculum vitae and a motivation letter in the enforced format - 1-1.5 pages, Calibri font size 11, 1.5 line spacing, 2.5 cm margins
Two letters of recommendation and the completed supplementary questionnaire indicating study-track preferences
Test results or certificate of the required level of English proficiency (C1, CAE, IELTS 7.0 or TOEFL 95), or a university-issued confirmation of a passed language course at the required level
selection_criteria: 'Masters may also offer full scholarships to the best-ranked students worldwide' - awards follow the ranking of applicants in each intake (EC students page)

'The selection, recruitment and monitoring of individual students fall under the sole responsibility of the EMJM consortium. Student selection must be organised transparently, impartially and equitably.' (Erasmus+ Programme Guide)
Scholarships are allocated per intake within the maximum number of scholarships funded in the grant agreement, and geographical balance must be maintained (Erasmus+ Programme Guide)
Czech-coordinated EPS: decisions are taken by a Selection Committee, announced 30 April for the 2026-2028 round, and applicants may appeal within 2 weeks to the EPS Programme Board for re-assessment
coverage: Travel, visa, installation and subsistence costs (Erasmus+ Programme Guide, student scholarship definition)
Participation costs, plus a contribution to travel, visa and a living allowance (EC students page)
Full tuition fees for scholarship holders, who cannot be charged tuition fees or other mandatory participation costs (Erasmus+ Programme Guide)
Czech-coordinated EPS: 'Full coverage of the Tuition Fee' (11,000 EUR Programme Country / 18 000 EUR Partner Country) and 'Living Allowances up to 24 months: 1,400 EUR per month (33,600 EUR)'
Insurance for scholarship holders (Czech-coordinated EPS consortium)
application_method: 'Students apply directly to the institution running their chosen programme' (EC students page)
'Search the course catalogue' - the EACEA Erasmus Mundus Catalogue, updated annually, listing the master's programmes currently supported by the European Union
'Visit the program's official website and directly contact the consortium for information on courses, application procedures, and scholarship availability' (EACEA catalogue)

Czech-coordinated EPS: apply online through the Charles University admissions system, with no application fee; the scholarship decision is automatic for anything filed before the 28 February scholarship cut-off
official.application_route: Shortlist a Czech-participating joint Master in the EACEA Erasmus Mundus Catalogue, then apply directly and only to that programme's own consortium portal with its own document set - there is no central EU application form for students.
official.study_mode: Full-time only - 'the scholarship can only be awarded in full, and to full-time students' (Erasmus+ Programme Guide)
official.citizenship_residency: No nationality or residency bar: 'Students from all over the world are welcome' and 'EMJM scholarships can be offered to students from all over the world'. The published split is between a Programme Country track (national of, or ordinarily resident / main activity of more than 12 months over the last five years in, an Erasmus+ Programme Country) and a Partner Country track (everyone else), which sets the tuition cap but not eligibility.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - students from all countries worldwide are eligible for both the programme and the scholarship; the Czech-coordinated consortium states it gives 'scholarships to students from all around the world' and that 'There is no limitation in terms of disciplines'.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: None at scheme level: 'There is no limitation in terms of disciplines' and any number of fields are funded. Each consortium sets its own subject entry requirement. Additional EU external-action scholarships (NDICI / IPA III) are reserved for students from targeted regions of the world - Western Balkans, Neighbourhood South, Asia, Central Asia, Middle East, Pacific, Sub-Saharan Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean - and follow the EU's Global Gateway priorities.
official.research_requirement: No research proposal is published as a scholarship requirement; the money follows academic ranking. A Master thesis is part of the programme itself ('periods of study, research, traineeship, thesis preparation and defence'), and the Czech-coordinated EPS consortium asks for a motivation letter (1-1.5 pages) plus a supplementary questionnaire on study-track preferences instead of a proposal.
official.duration: '1 to 2 academic years (60, 90 or 120 ECTS credits)' at scheme level; the scholarship runs for the whole programme (12, 18 or 24 months) and may be shortened only by recognition of prior learning, with a minimum of one academic year. Czech example: the EPS programme is a two-year, four-semester Master with living allowances paid up to 24 months.
official.description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are 'prestigious international masters, jointly designed and delivered by a group of higher education institutions', involving at least three institutions from at least three different countries, and typically including periods of study, research, traineeship, thesis preparation and defence. Czech universities take part in these consortia, and the European Commission funds 'full scholarships ... for the best students' worldwide, covering participation costs and contributing to travel, visa and a living allowance. Graduates receive either a single joint degree or multiple national degrees.
official.region: Europe - mobility in at least two countries, at least one of which must be an EU Member State or third country associated to the Programme, with Czech universities among the participating institutions; applicants come from all over the world
official.program_type: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EMJM) - integrated transnational Master delivered by a consortium of at least three higher education institutions from three different countries, leading to a joint or multiple degree
official.english_requirement: The EU publishes no single language rule - each consortium sets its own. As the published Czech example, the Czech-coordinated EPS (Vaclav Havel) consortium requires 'C1; CAE; IELTS 7.0; TOEFL 95' for non-native English speakers and accepts 'language confirmation/passed language course of the required language level skills issued by a university'.

not_confirmed: deadline_central / deadline_central_display - the Commission publishes no central student deadline, only an October-January window, with exact dates set per programme
A scheme-wide English test score or MOI rule (set by each consortium; only the Czech-coordinated EPS values are published)

The Czech-country landing page held in the catalogue record (https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/opportunities/individuals/students/erasmus-mundus-joint-masters/czech-republic) returns HTTP 404 on two attempts; the parent Commission student page was used instead
A complete, current list of every EMJM with a Czech partner institution - the EACEA catalogue country filter is client-side and its keyword search did not filter server-side
Itemised travel, visa and installation amounts - the Programme Guide publishes them inside the single EUR 1 400/month unit cost rather than as separate figures
Student-level award criteria weightings - the Programme Guide only states that the best-ranked students are selected by the consortium
verification.notes: Award value taken from the Erasmus+ Programme Guide (version 1 of 12.11.2025, part of the 2026 Call for Proposals), Lot 1 Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters, 'Student scholarships': 'The scholarship is calculated as: 1 400 Euros/month x DS'; cross-checked against the Czech-coordinated EPS consortium page stating 1 400 EUR per month for up to 24 months plus full tuition coverage, and against the Commission student page stating full scholarships cover participation costs and contribute to travel, visa and a living allowance.

applicant_utility.summary: This is not one scholarship with one deadline: it is the EU funding layer on top of a set of jointly delivered Master programmes, so you apply to a single consortium's portal and only the best-ranked applicants in that intake are funded. The published value is EUR 1 400 per month for the whole programme (12, 18 or 24 months) plus full tuition, because the Programme Guide bars projects from charging tuition fees or application fees to scholarship holders. What decides your outcome is not the Commission calendar but the consortium's own round, and at the Czech-coordinated Vaclav Havel programme the funding window shut at the end of February while self-funded applications were still being accepted well into April. Apply to several consortia, not just the Czech one, because each consortium runs its own ranking and scholarship quota.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent bachelor graduates with a strong transcript, English at C1, and a clear reason for a two-country Master who can file inside a programme's February funding window.
application_readiness_checklist: Shortlist three or four EMJMs that include a Czech university in the EACEA catalogue, and confirm on each programme's own site that the current intake actually funds EMJM scholarships - the catalogue warns some listed masters no longer do.

Work out which track you fall into before you write anything: nationality and where you have lived/studied/worked for more than 12 months in the last five years decides the Programme-Country or Partner-Country route, which changes the tuition cap (EUR 11,000 vs EUR 18,000 at the Czech-coordinated programme).
Check you have never held an EMJM, EMJMD, Erasmus Mundus Master Course or Erasmus Mundus Joint Doctorate scholarship - any of them disqualifies you.

Order your English evidence now if your test is old or missing: a university-issued confirmation of a passed language course at the required level is accepted in place of IELTS/TOEFL at the Czech-coordinated programme, but it still takes weeks to obtain.
Start translation and residence-proof paperwork early - both diplomas, both transcripts and the proof of residence dated within 12 months of the deadline are the classic last-minute failures.

Follow the individual programme's calendar rather than a generic EU deadline (results are typically announced around the end of April for a February cut-off), and plan the compulsory two-country mobility and visa sequencing before you apply
common_rejection_risks: Filing after the consortium's scholarship cut-off but before its general deadline - at the Czech-coordinated Vaclav Havel programme anything arriving after midnight CET on 28 February is automatically routed to the self-funding round and drops out of scholarship selection entirely.
Residence proof dated more than 12 months before the deadline, or an untranslated second diploma/transcript; the requirement covers both previous studies, not only the degree you are applying with.
Applying to a programme that has run out of EU funding for the current intake, since inclusion in the EACEA catalogue does not guarantee a scholarship this year.
Nationality quota: no more than 10% of a project's scholarships may go to candidates of the same nationality, so applicants from the largest sending countries compete for a capped slice.
A previous Erasmus Mundus scholarship, part-time study, or heavy recognition of prior learning - the scholarship is only paid in full, to full-time students, for the full programme duration.
Missing a compulsory mobility element in the study plan, since every enrolled student must complete two study periods in two countries, at least one in an EU or associated country.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The EU unit cost of EUR 1 400 per month is the scholarship contribution covering tuition, travel, visa, installation and subsistence together, so anything above it stays with the applicant: rent deposits and above-allowance housing in Prague, Leiden, Krakow or Barcelona, return flights for personal travel, extracurricular trips and team-building events (the Czech-coordinated consortium states students pay their own expenses for those, mainly travelling), research/laptop costs, and any dependant or family costs. Non-scholarship holders carry the full tuition themselves, which the same consortium prices at EUR 11,000 (Programme Country track) or EUR 18,000 (Partner Country track) for the two years.
document_audit: Two diplomas are needed, not one: the completed (or in-progress) Bachelor/Master plus a second completed Bachelor's or the high-school diploma, all translated.
Both transcripts of all previous studies must be translated - a translated degree certificate alone will not complete the file.
The proof of residence has a hard 12-month freshness rule and must come from the PRADO-listed document types or from the candidate's employer/study institution.

Application-form items carry no waiver: the motivation letter must follow the enforced format (1-1.5 pages, Calibri 11, 1.5 line spacing, 2.5 cm margins), the supplementary questionnaire on study-track preferences is a separate compulsory file, and two recommendation letters are required even if you already hold a relevant Master's degree.

English evidence must be a test score or a university-issued confirmation of a passed language course at the required level - never a self-declaration - and it is only required for non-native speakers.
The consortium publishes a model Student Agreement with the rights and obligations you sign on enrolment; read it before accepting an offer.
alerts: The funding window and the admission window are different: in the Czech-coordinated example the scholarship decision was tied to a 28 February cut-off while self-funding applications ran on to 30 April, so a late file can win a place and lose the money.

Funding is time-limited by project: the Czech-coordinated programme states its scholarships run to 2031, and the EACEA catalogue is rebuilt each year, so a consortium you spotted last cycle may no longer be EU-funded.

Country-specific pages in the Commission's site structure are being retired (the Czech Republic page in the catalogue record now returns 404), so verify dates on the Commission student page and on the consortium's own site.
Scholarship money follows a strict eligibility test on previous Erasmus Mundus funding - if you have ever held one, you cannot hold another EMJM scholarship.
Erasmus Mundus never charges an application fee and EACEA publishes a scam/fraud warning; any 'agent' asking for payment to process an application is not part of the scheme.
Top-up scholarships for students from targeted world regions are allocated by EU external-action priorities, so an applicant from a region outside those priorities cannot count on one.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply online directly in the consortium's own admissions portal (the Czech-coordinated programme routes through the Charles University admissions system), upload the full translated document set plus the supplementary questionnaire before that programme's funding cut-off, then the consortium's selection committee ranks applicants and publishes results, with a two-week appeal route against a negative decision.
